hashed.why: AUTOMATION-165. THE HOUSE RULES THEMSELVES, and they live outside src/+tests/ so no walk of the discovery roots reaches them. Break FSHW-CLAIM-001 or delete a rule and, before this was declared, a green earned while the rule held still reported Applies. The directory is declared rather than a glob so the .fsproj is covered too: the compile list decides which rules are in the assembly at all.
AUTOMATION-165. The per-file coverage floors. Lower one and a verdict earned under the higher floor must stop applying; hashing it is the only thing that makes that true.
AUTOMATION-165. The coverage collector's include/exclude filters. Widen an exclusion and files stop being measured at all, which moves every floor beneath it without touching the floors file.
AUTOMATION-165. The lint rules the lint plugin enforces. Disabling one changes what the check concludes about an unchanged tree.
AUTOMATION-165. The restore-only project that materializes the FSharpLint analyzer the check loads. Move its pin and a different set of findings is produced from the same source.

notInputs.reason: AUTOMATION-165. Release prose. No plugin reads it, so it cannot change what a check concludes — and re-earning a full unfiltered verdict for a paragraph about work that was already gated buys nothing. Stated here rather than merely absent, so the exclusion is reviewable instead of invisible. NOTE the per-package CHANGELOGs under src/ ARE hashed: they are inside the discovery roots, and carving holes in that walk is a bigger hazard than the re-gate.
AUTOMATION-165. Configures the RELEASE tagger, which runs after a verdict is earned and never contributes to one. Changing it changes what gets published, not what the check concludes.

excluded.reason: AUTOMATION-158. 64 END-TO-END tests (IntegrationTests 58, PluginTimeout 2, PluginActivityConcurrency 2, TestPruneStorm 1, ProcessHelperTimeout 1) that stand up REAL infrastructure — live plugin hosts and daemons over temp repos, real file watchers, real child `dotnet` processes — and assert on WALL-CLOCK behaviour: plugin timeouts, process reaping, activity concurrency, TestPrune under a storm of edits. Run from inside the daemon that IS the gate, they nest a daemon in a daemon and contend for the box the outer run is being timed on, so their timing assertions become a function of machine load rather than of the code. Their coverage is excluded for the same family of reasons (no Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage reference: SDK-reflection paths fire nondeterministically and would make the ratchet flaky — see CLAUDE.md). NOT UNGATED: `mise run test-integration` runs them, and CI's reusable workflow runs a solution-wide `dotnet test` that includes them, so they must be green to merge — just not from inside the warm-daemon inner loop. The exclusion is DECLARED: it is logged on every green load and recorded in verdict.json's `scope.excluded`, so a consumer of a `kind: full` verdict sees the gap instead of inferring completeness from a count.
